title: 2x2 ribbed scarf
subtitle: Wide knit and purl columns for a scarf with strong vertical texture.
excerpt: A flat scarf worked in 2x2 rib on 5 mm needles with aran yarn, finishing at 20 cm wide and 175 cm long. The two-stitch columns produce a bolder, more defined fabric than 1x1 rib, with similar stretch and reversibility.
sourceNotes: 2x2 ribbing is a standard fabric structure documented throughout Weldon's Practical Knitter for neckwear, cuffs, and scarves. Cornelia Mee, A Manual of Knitting and Crochet (1846), Internet Archive.
heroPrompt: A 2x2 ribbed scarf in deep burgundy aran wool, showing the bold vertical columns, with the scarf loosely folded to display both the ribbed face and the stretch width.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts x 26 rows = 10 x 10 cm in 2x2 rib on 5 mm needles, measured unstretched.

glossaryTerms.definition: A knitting fabric formed by alternating two knit stitches and two purl stitches across each row, with the columns aligned above themselves every row. Produces a stretchy, reversible fabric with wider columns than 1x1 rib.
A cast-on method using the tail and working yarn together to form an elastic, neat edge.
A cast-off worked in pattern with more slack than the standard cast-off, so the finished edge matches the elasticity of the rib body.

content.text: This is a flat scarf worked from one short end to the other in
2x2 rib

on 5 mm needles with aran-weight yarn, finishing at 20 cm wide and 175 cm long when measured flat and unstretched. The two-stitch columns make a bolder vertical fabric than 1x1 rib and hold their shape well in aran yarn.

Flat construction suits a ribbed scarf because the rib pattern is the same on both sides: there is no need to manage a seam or a circular join. The aran weight makes the work go quickly, and the extra warmth suits a scarf worn close to the neck in cold weather. The finished scarf uses about 200 g (360 m / 393 yards) of aran-weight yarn.
What you need

items.name: Aran-weight wool or wool-blend yarn
items.substitutions: Any aran yarn. Wool or wool-blend recovers best after stretching.

content.text: Gauge

18 sts x 26 rows = 10 x 10 cm in 2x2 rib on 5 mm needles, measured unstretched after the swatch has rested off the needles for at least ten minutes. Each stitch off gauge changes the finished width by about 1.1 cm: at 16 sts per 10 cm the scarf finishes about 22 cm wide; at 20 sts it finishes about 18 cm wide.
Stitches used
K (knit), P (purl). In 2x2 rib, work K2, P2 across. The stitch count of 36 is a multiple of 4, so the rib starts and ends with K2.
Pattern
Cast on
Use the
long-tail cast-on
to place 36 stitches. For 5 mm needles (circumference approximately 15.7 mm) and 36 stitches: tail_cm = (15.7 x 36) / 10 + 15 = 72 cm. Leave a tail of at least 72 cm before making the slip knot.
Stitch count check-in: 36 stitches after the cast-on.
Body
Every row: (K2, P2) to end. (36 sts)
Repeat until the scarf measures 175 cm from the cast-on edge, measured flat and unstretched. This takes approximately 455 rows. At the halfway mark (about 87 cm), count the stitches: still 36.
Cast off
Use a
stretchy cast off
worked in pattern (knit the knit stitches, purl the purl stitches) to match the body elasticity. Work loosely.
Common faults

Columns breaking up or running unevenly. Usually caused by losing track of which stitch is knit and which is purl on a new row. Read the stitches as they sit: a V-shape is a knit, a horizontal bump is a purl.
Stitch count creeping up. Yarn left in the wrong position at the transition from purl to knit makes an accidental yarn-over. Carry the yarn firmly to the back before every knit stitch.
Cast-off edge too tight. Work the cast-off on a needle one size larger or two sizes larger if needed to match the body width.
Finishing
Weave in ends along the rib columns on the wrong side. Do not block flat: lay the finished piece on a towel, pat to shape, and leave to dry. Blocking removes the stretch that makes rib useful.
Care
Handwash in cool water and lay flat to dry. Support the wet weight of the scarf when lifting it out of the water; do not wring or hang while wet.
What to try next
The next step is the seed-stitch scarf. It uses the same knit and purl stitches in an alternating pattern. The result is a bumpy, non-stretchy fabric that lies flat without any border.
